P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes, a forced-conversion regime applies. Foreign currency earned by Myanmar residents must be deposited with authorised banks in Myanmar, and a set percentage converted into kyat within one working day of receipt. The conversion is at official rates, which have been far below market. For export earnings the share was 65% (2022), cut to 50%, 35% and 25%, and then to 15% from 1 January 2026 (CBM Notification 2/2026). Myanmar also remains on the FATF 'call for action' list (June 2026), so foreign banks and platforms apply enhanced due diligence.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Resident nationals and resident foreigners are taxed on worldwide income. Residence is based on days present in the income year (reported as 183 days; not captured). Other income, including professional and business income, is taxed at progressive rates of 1% to 25%. Since 1 October 2023, non-resident citizens are taxed on salaries received abroad, at the lower of the progressive rates or 2%; their other income is taxed at 10%. Tax on income received in foreign currency must be paid in that currency.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: There is no VAT; commercial tax, a turnover tax, applies instead. Most services are taxed at 5%, and internet-services income at 15%. Manufacturers, traders and service providers above annual sales of MMK 50,000,000 must register (2024 Union Taxation Law). Treatment of services exported to foreign clients was not captured.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: No comprehensive personal-data law was found in force. Cybersecurity Law No. 1/2025 took effect on 30 July 2025 (Notification 113/2025). It requires digital platform providers to retain user information, including personal data, for three years, and requires approval to provide VPN services. Platforms with over 100,000 Myanmar users must register.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; PayPal is not available; Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (2) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (3) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
